title.narrative: Strengthening the System of Protected Areas and Improvement of its Financial Sustainability

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

This project will deliver direct and indirect benefits to communities and individuals in buffer zones of the five prioritized protected areas, and primarily in the communities of San Carlos del Apa, San Alfredo, Jose Felix Lopez, Presidente Franco, Ybycui, Mbuyapey, San Roque, Quindy, Carapegua, and Acahay, targeting 22,841 women and 21,848 men. Enhanced management effectiveness of the Sub-System of Protected Areas in Paraguay from a well-financed system will help to secure the ecosystems and associated goods and services these systems provide to local communities and the broader society in terms of water security, food, medicine, fuel, food, clean air, and carbon sequestration. The 780,833 metric tons of CO2e to be sequestered as a result of project interventions on 120,991 hectares of PAs will make an important contribution to global efforts to reduce Green House Gases in the best interest of mankind.The project expects to foster an economic environment and strengthen livelihoods of the local communities through the the Training of Trainers Program In Sustainable Alternative Livelihoods in PA Buffer Zones’ and will provide micro-business incubation support to 10 demonstration projects based on the alternative livelihoods training provided to communities in the PA buffer zones. At the institutional level, the Directorate General for the Protection and Conservation of Biodiversity will benefit from a strengthened policy and legal framework while its personnel will benefit from training in the interpretation and implementation of the Revised Park Rangers Law and the technical skills needed for proper field monitoring of PAs. This Directorate will also benefit from a new module of the Environmental Information System (SIAM) to be able to link and integrate PA monitoring data and METT results to the system. Communities in the buffer zones of the five prioritized protected areas will benefit from micro-business start-up and incubation support via 10 demonstration projects based on the alternative livelihoods training that will be provided prior. Key organizations in Government Agencies, NGOs and Civil Society will benefit from training in the design, governance, and implementation of PFPs. Policy makers (in the legislature and the executive branches of government) will benefit from policy dialogues while local communities will benefit from participation in Consultative Groups to be established for the five prioritized PAs. The global conservation and PA management community will benefit from lessons learned on PFP development and management to be presented at regional and global events, as appropriate.
To strengthen the protected area management system and financial sustainability of the public protected areas in Paraguay.
